content: The analgesic effects of ibuprofen-codeine sustained-release tablets have been studied in the context of postoperative and cancer-related pain management. Morphine sulfate sustained-release tablets and immediate-release morphine sulfate solutions have been compared in placebo-blinded studies for chronic pain in advanced cancer patients. Dosage equivalency between oxymorphone extended-release and oxycodone controlled-release has been established in randomized controlled trials for cancer pain patients. Comparative clinical efficacy and safety of novel controlled-release formulations of oxycodone and hydromorphone have been evaluated for cancer pain treatment. Randomized, double-blind studies have compared OROS® hydromorphone and controlled-release morphine for chronic cancer pain control. Controlled-release oxycodone and morphine have been assessed for their effectiveness in cancer-related pain. Two sustained-release morphine preparations have been compared for pain management in advanced cancer patients. Morphine and oxycodone hydrochloride have been studied for their roles in cancer pain management. Immediate-release versus sustained-release morphine has been evaluated for dose finding during the initiation of morphine therapy in cancer patients. Celecoxib's impact on survival in advanced non-small cell lung cancer patients has been investigated in a double-blind randomized clinical trial. Direct conversion from tramadol to tapentadol prolonged-release has been studied for moderate to severe chronic malignant tumor-related pain. WHO guidelines provide comprehensive recommendations for the pharmacological and radiotherapeutic management of cancer pain in adults and adolescents. Combined fentanyl-TTS and tramadol have been shown to improve cancer pain treatment. Morphine versus methadone has been compared for pain management in advanced cancer patients receiving home care. Ketorolac and diclofenac have been evaluated in double-blind studies for cancer pain. Controlled-release oxycodone and morphine have been compared in randomized, double-blind, parallel-group studies for cancer pain treatment. Oral ketorolac and diclofenac have been assessed for their analgesic efficacy and toxicity in cancer pain. Tapentadol prolonged-release has been studied for managing moderate to severe chronic malignant tumor-related pain. Breakthrough pain has been defined, and its prevalence and characteristics have been studied. Opioid switching has been systematically reviewed for its role in cancer pain management. Evidence-based recommendations for opioid analgesics in cancer pain treatment have been provided by the EAPC. Morphine depot tablets have been compared with conventional morphine tablets for cancer pain treatment. Pharmacokinetics and clinical efficacy of oral morphine solution and controlled-release morphine tablets have been studied in cancer patients. Continuous subcutaneous and intravenous hydromorphone infusions have been compared for cancer pain management. Buprenorphine has been evaluated for managing opioid withdrawal. Methadone at tapered doses has been studied for opioid withdrawal management. Corticosteroids have been assessed as adjuvant analgesics in cancer pain. Oral methylprednisolone has been studied for its effects in terminal cancer patients. Methylprednisolone has been evaluated as palliative therapy for female terminal cancer patients. Prednisolone has been studied in terminal breast and bronchogenic cancer. Methylprednisolone sodium succinate has been assessed for its impact on quality of life in preterminal cancer patients. Dexamethasone has been studied in combination with metoclopramide for chronic nausea in advanced cancer patients. Dexamethasone has been shown to reduce cancer-related fatigue in advanced cancer patients. Methylprednisolone has been evaluated for its effects on pain, fatigue, and appetite loss in advanced cancer patients using opioids. Amitriptyline, gabapentin, and pregabalin have been compared for neuropathic cancer pain in randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled studies. Neuropathic pain in cancer has been reviewed for its management strategies. Outcome reporting in industry-sponsored trials of gabapentin for off-label use has been critically analyzed. Differences in reporting of analyses in internal company documents versus published trial reports have been studied in industry-sponsored trials. The management of cancer pain has been addressed in ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines. Bisphosphonates have been studied for relieving pain secondary to bone metastases. Ibandronate has been compared with single-dose radiotherapy for localized metastatic bone pain in prostate cancer. Intravenous ibandronate has been shown to reduce skeletal complications in breast cancer patients with bone metastases. Oral ibandronate has been studied for its ability to reduce skeletal complications in breast cancer patients with metastatic bone disease.
